item.text: {"results":[{"pair_id":"J00730","case1_error":"Uses remaining water instead of allowable water loss, then unjustifiably subtracts identical jump counts.","case2_error":"Gives unsupported final total 960 after the correct formula 120 + (6 × 120), which yields 840.","reason":"Case 1 constructs erroneous relations; case 2 supplies an incorrect final number after a correct formula.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J00731","case1_error":"Subtracts the six-inch clearance from rim height instead of adding it.","case2_error":"Assigns the brother’s lifting capacity to Felix, ignoring Felix’s own weight and lifting multiplier.","reason":"Case 1 reverses the clearance direction; case 2 substitutes another person’s lifting relationship.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J00732","case1_error":"Explicitly evaluates 30 + 35 + 46 as 101 instead of 111.","case2_error":"Subtracts money from length and constructs an incorrect remaining-length expression; its final 10000 also disagrees with that expression.","reason":"Case 1 is numerical evaluation of a correct sum. Case 2 has invalid quantity relations regardless of the field dimensions’ interpretation.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J00733","case1_error":"Uses the original nine T-shirts as the tripling base, although the wording leaves that referent ambiguous.","case2_error":"Supplies unsupported final total 680 after a correct formula that yields 1220.","reason":"Case 1 depends on an ambiguous referent for “triple the number”; case 2 clearly gives an incorrect final number after a correct formula.","judgment":"uncertain"},{"pair_id":"J00734","case1_error":"Treats the brother’s entire pre-purchase balance as Michael’s gift and answers Michael’s initial money instead of the brother’s.","case2_error":"Represents “$1000 less” with +1000 instead of −1000.","reason":"Case 1 conflates the gift with the recipient’s balance and changes the requested quantity; case 2 reverses the stated monetary adjustment.","judgment":"different"}]}
